name: ifetch
mechanism: instruction.fetch (L0 replacement when a loop is slightly larger than the L0)
question: How many lines miss per pass when straight-line code that is looped is a little larger than the L0 (224 to 392 lines)?
why: deepgemm_fp8_dense_08 (H100 full GPU, sim / ncu 1.45; $A/fg-line-cold/attrib1/pcs): its loop touches about 274 code lines per SM; the engine's L0 (LRU, 224 lines per SM) misses every line on every iteration (11.6 k cycles of fetch wait per warp, 6-9 per line visit), the hardware has no_instruction samples on 0.05 % of those lines' time. The v1 / v2 data already show the regime: warm cycles per instruction 1.00 up to 1792 instructions (224 lines), 1.156 at 2048 (256 lines; about 320 cycles per pass, the cell was a transition cell outside the fits), 2.16 from 3072 on (392 lines, every line streams). An LRU thrashes completely from the first line over capacity.
probe: tools/microbench/ifetch/probe (unchanged kernels; bodies regenerated for the new sizes): ifetch.line.n<N>.w1 for N = 1792, 1856, 1920, 1984, 2048, 2112, 2176, 2240, 2304, 2432, 2560, 2816, 3072; ifetch.line.n<N>.w4 for N = 1792, 2048, 2304, 2560 (four warps on the same code). K = 4 passes per launch, ncu --cache-control all as v1; warm = passes 1..3.
derivation: per N the warm T_pass (median) and cpi = T / N as model.py; missed lines per pass = (T - N) / c with c = the per-line extra of the 3072 cell ((T - N) / lines).
prediction_of_the_engine (LRU of capacit: cpi = the 3072-cell value (2.16 on h100) for every N whose line count plus loop overhead exceeds 224, i.e. from 1856 on.

reading.R1: cpi within 5 % of the 3072 value from the first size over capacity -> the engine's policy holds and the deepgemm excess is elsewhere.
reading.R2: otherwise the curve missed-lines(N) is the result: its slope near capacity (1 line per line over capacity = lines that do not fit are fetched each time and nothing is evicted; 2 = pairs displace each other) and the size at which every line misses; a replacement rule is proposed in an addendum (post hoc) and checked on the w4 cells and the existing jump cells.

not_allowed: no value from full-GPU error; no per-kernel rule.

reading.R2: the engine's prediction (full cost from the first size over 224 lines) is wrong on both devices. H100 warm T - N: 21 up to 248 lines, then 340 / 732 / 1040 / 1460 / 1852 / 2580 at 256 / 264 / 272 / 280 / 288 / 304 lines and 9.3 cycles per line for every line from 320 lines on, i.e. 34 / 76 / 110 / 155 / 197 / 275 missed lines. B300: 22 up to 240, 9 missed lines at 248, then 35 / 80 / 122 / 155 / 200 / 275, every line from 320 on at 16.0 per line. Four warps on the same code: the same numbers.
reading.rule (post hoc): five misses per line beyond about 248 and saturation 64 lines later is what a 4-way set-associative cache of 64 sets (256 lines, 32 KiB, set = line number mod 64, LRU inside a set) does with a cyclic walk over contiguous lines: every line over capacity overloads one set, and an overloaded set misses on all five of its lines; the loop's own 8-10 lines outside the body share the cache. Predicted missed lines 5 x (lines + 8 - 256): 40 / 80 / 120 / 160 / 200 / 280, all from 312 on.
reading.check on cells the rule's constants do n: B300 was not used to set them and gives the same curve; the earlier capacity (28672 B) came from the last plateau cell of the coarser v1 sweep (1792 instructions).

addenda.installed: instruction.fetch on both devices: capacity_l0_bytes 32768, l0_ways 4 (new field), experimental. Engine: the L0 is a per-set LRU.
addenda.not_modelled: the per-line cost at full thrash (9.3 / 16.0 cycles measured) is left to the existing stream fields.
